Definition: Whether primary laws, acts, or legal instruments exist that establish authority for cross-government data sharing and govern the data exchange system
Comments: POPIA (Protection of Personal Information Act) effective July 1 2021 with Information Regulator enforcement powers. SITA Act (Act 88 of 1998) mandates Minimum Interoperability Standards (MIOS v6.0) for all government ICT. Public Service Act and Regulations require MIOS compliance. These collectively enable and govern cross-government data sharing.

revised_comments: South Africa's cross-government data sharing rests on an established, multi-instrument legal basis. The State Information Technology Agency Act, 1998 (Act 88 of 1998) gives SITA a statutory mandate to set and certify interoperability standards between government information systems. The Public Service Act, 1994, together with Public Service Regulations, 2016 (regulation 97), obliges all government departments to comply with the Minimum Interoperability Standards (MIOS v6.0), which prescribe data format and technical standards for exchanging data between government systems (Government-to-Government, Government-to-Business and Government-to-Citizen). The Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA), in force since July 2021, governs the collection, processing and cross-border transfer of personal data, with enforcement powers vested in the Information Regulator. Collectively these instruments establish and govern authority for cross-government data sharing. A further, data-exchange-specific legal and governance framework is being developed alongside the National Treasury's MzansiXchange pilot, launched in October 2025 to build a federated government data exchange platform.
